statement: Chinese regulators told the approved buyers to keep the licensed H200 hardware in Hong Kong, outside mainland China's customs border, to support domestic chipmakers.
why: A regulatory instruction to park the hardware offshore, at buyers that reportedly lack Hong Kong data centers, throttles how quickly approved volumes convert into deployed capacity and real orders.

impact.mechanism: Beijing steering licensed chips outside the mainland to favor domestic chipmakers limits deployable siting for merchant GPUs and slows the conversion of export approvals into repeat demand.

evidence.excerpt: 'Beijing wants them to keep the hardware outside mainland China to support the growth of domestic chipmakers'

confidence.basis: Anonymously sourced FT reporting relayed by Reuters, which says it could not immediately verify; syndicated copies are not independent corroboration.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: magnitude 1 -> 2; sources: Reuters (syndicated on Yahoo Finance)
